title: English, Class 9
subject: English
description: NCERT Grade 9 English, chapter by chapter.

chapters.title: How I Taught My Grandmother to Read
chapters.summary: In this chapter: lesson 1: life in a north karnataka village; lesson 2: kashi yatre and the grandmother's love of stories; lesson 3: the grandmother waits for the next episode; lesson 4: the grandmother tells her life story.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Life in a North Karnataka Village

activities.prompt: What news and stories were waiting for Kaveri’s family when the bus arrived?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Village News and Kannada Stories
activities.body: Kaveri lived in a north Karnataka village with her grandparents. Poor transport delayed newspapers. The morning paper reached the family only in the afternoon. The weekly magazine arrived one day late. Everyone waited eagerly for the bus. It brought newspapers, magazines and post. Triveni wrote Kannada stories. Her easy-to-read style was convincing. Her stories dealt with difficult problems in ordinary lives. People continued to appreciate her novels forty years later.
keyPoints: Life with grandparents in a north Karnataka village
Late delivery because of poor transport
Triveni's popular and lasting Kannada stories
activities.explanation: This card introduces village life and Triveni's writing.

activities.prompt: Why does Kaveri’s family receive its morning paper only in the afternoon?
steps: The village transport system is poor, so newspapers travel slowly.
This is why newspapers reach the village late.
The bus brings newspapers, so the paper must wait for it.
Therefore, the family receives the morning paper only in the afternoon.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Kaveri's Family
activities.prompt: Who lived with Kaveri in the village?
options: her teachers
her cousins
her grandparents
her friends
activities.explanation: The lesson says Kaveri lived with her grandparents.

activities.title: The Weekly Magazine
activities.prompt: The weekly magazine arrived ______ day late.
activities.hint: Think about how long the magazine was delayed.
activities.explanation: The weekly magazine arrived one day late.

activities.title: Village Deliveries
activities.prompt: Match each item with its detail from the lesson.
activities.explanation: Each pair matches a delivery item with the detail given.

activities.title: Triveni's Work
activities.prompt: Which description identifies Triveni correctly?
options: a bus driver in north Karnataka
a newspaper seller in the village
a popular writer in Kannada
a weekly magazine delivery worker
activities.explanation: The lesson identifies Triveni as a popular Kannada writer.

activities.title: Triveni's Story in Time Order
activities.prompt: Put these events in the correct time order.
items: Triveni wrote her stories
Triveni died when she was very young
People appreciated her novels forty years later
activities.explanation: She wrote during her life, then died, then gained lasting appreciation.

activities.title: Triveni's Writing
activities.prompt: Which description fits Triveni's writing and stories?
options: Hard to read, doubtful and confusing
Quick to read, weak and puzzling
Clear, simple and dull
Easy to read, convincing and interesting
activities.explanation: Her style was easy to read and convincing, and her stories were interesting.

activities.prompt: Everyone in Kaveri’s family waits eagerly for the bus. Why do they wait?
options: They want the newspapers, magazines and post that it brings.
They hope the village transport system will improve soon.
They need the bus to visit their grandparents.
They enjoy seeing the bus arrive in the village.

why.They hope the village transport system w: This mistake assumes that waiting can improve the transport system.
why.They need the bus to visit their grandpa: This mistake treats Kaveri’s grandparents as people living elsewhere.
why.They enjoy seeing the bus arrive in the: This mistake thinks the family waits only to watch the bus.

activities.explanation: This is right because the bus brings newspapers, magazines and post.

activities.prompt: Everyone waits eagerly for the village bus. How do they feel when it arrives?
options: Excited, because the bus brings things they want.
Angry, because the bus brings nothing they need.
Worried, because the bus will leave very soon.
Bored, because nobody is waiting for the bus.

why.Angry, because the bus brings nothing th: This mistake ignores that the bus brings newspapers, magazines and post.
why.Worried, because the bus will leave very: This mistake assumes the bus’s departure is their main concern.
why.Bored, because nobody is waiting for the: This mistake ignores that everyone waited eagerly for the bus.

activities.explanation: This is right because eager waiting and useful deliveries suggest excitement.

activities.prompt: Triveni’s story describes an ordinary person’s difficult problem. What will a reader likely do?
options: Keep reading, because Triveni’s stories are always interesting.
Stop reading, because difficult problems are always simple.
Stop reading, because daily-life problems are not interesting.
Stop reading, because interesting stories must end quickly.

why.Stop reading, because difficult problems: This mistake confuses difficult problems with simple ones.
why.Stop reading, because daily-life problem: This mistake assumes daily-life stories cannot interest readers.
why.Stop reading, because interesting storie: This mistake believes interesting stories should end quickly.

activities.explanation: This is right because Triveni’s stories were always very interesting.

activities.prompt: Triveni’s writing is easy to read and convincing. What does “convincing” show?
options: The reader trusts what the writer says.
The reader expects every problem to be difficult.
The reader knows many people like the writer.
The reader finds every word very interesting.

why.The reader expects every problem to be d: This mistake confuses convincing writing with difficult subjects.
why.The reader knows many people like the wr: This mistake confuses convincing writing with being popular.
why.The reader finds every word very interes: This mistake confuses convincing writing with being interesting.

activities.explanation: This is right because convincing writing makes readers trust the writer.

activities.prompt: Triveni died very young, but people appreciated her novels forty years later. Why?
options: Her stories stayed interesting and tackled ordinary people’s difficult problems.
She lived long enough to gain many new readers.
Her novels became popular because nobody read them.
People forgot how difficult her stories had been.

why.She lived long enough to gain many new r: This mistake ignores that Triveni died very young.
why.Her novels became popular because nobody: This mistake wrongly connects popularity with having no readers.
why.People forgot how difficult her stories: This mistake ignores that people continued to appreciate her novels.

activities.explanation: This is right because her stories remained interesting and dealt with difficult problems.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Kashi Yatre and the Grandmother's Love of Stories

activities.prompt: Could Kashi Yatre reveal what love and sacrifice truly mean?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Stories that stay with us
activities.body: Kashi Yatre began as a serial about an old lady who wished to visit Kashi or Varanasi. Her struggle to reach Kashi, and an orphan girl's love story, shape the tale. She gave away her savings without visiting Kashi. Meanwhile, Kaveri read each Wednesday episode to her grandmother, who later repeated the whole text from memory.
keyPoints: Kashi Yatre first appeared as a serial.
The old lady valued the orphan girl's happiness.
Kaveri shared magazine episodes with her grandmother.
activities.explanation: You can now connect the journey, the orphan girl, and the grandmother's love of stories.

activities.prompt: Kaveri’s grandmother cannot read. How can she still remember a whole magazine story?
steps: Kaveri reads each Wednesday’s episode aloud because a new part has arrived.
She listens closely because later she repeats the whole text from memory.
So she can remember a story without reading the printed words herself.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The grandmother's love of stories
activities.body: Kaveri's grandmother had never been to school and could not read. The magazine came every Wednesday, and Kaveri read the next episode to her grandmother. Later, the grandmother repeated the whole text from memory. These moments show the important place of stories in the grandmother's life.
keyPoints: Kaveri's grandmother could not read.
Kaveri read the next episode to her.
The grandmother later remembered the whole text.
activities.explanation: You can see how Kaveri's care made stories special for her grandmother.

activities.title: First appearance
activities.prompt: What did Kashi Yatre first appear as?
options: A serial.
A novel.
A poem.
A play.
activities.explanation: Kashi Yatre first appeared as a serial before becoming a novel.

activities.title: Another story
activities.prompt: What else did the novel show?
options: An orphan girl falling in love.
An old lady learning to read.
A family moving into Kashi.
A shopkeeper selling clothes.
activities.explanation: The novel also showed an orphan girl falling in love.

activities.title: Story day
activities.prompt: The magazine came every ______, and Kaveri read the next episode.
activities.hint: Name the day when the magazine came.
activities.explanation: The magazine came every Wednesday, when Kaveri shared the next episode.

activities.title: People and events
activities.prompt: Match each person with what happened in the lesson.
pairs: had no money for her wedding
activities.explanation: You matched each person with the correct event from the story.

activities.title: From episode to memory
activities.prompt: Put these moments in the correct order.
items: The magazine came every Wednesday.
Kaveri read the next episode to her grandmother.
Her grandmother repeated the whole text from memory.
activities.explanation: The magazine arrived first, Kaveri read the episode, and her grandmother later remembered it.

activities.title: The old lady's choice
activities.prompt: What did the old lady value more than worship at Kashi?
options: The orphan girl's happiness.
The old lady's journey.
The orphan girl's savings.
The grandmother's school.
activities.explanation: The old lady valued the orphan girl's happiness more than worship at Kashi.

activities.prompt: The old lady gives away all her savings without visiting Kashi. Why did she do this?
options: She valued the orphan girl’s happiness more than worship at Kashi.
She believed Kashi could never make anyone feel happy.
She wanted the orphan girl to lose her own wedding.
She had already visited Kashi and needed no savings.

why.She believed Kashi could never make anyo: This confuses her wish to visit Kashi with not caring about Kashi.
why.She wanted the orphan girl to lose her o: This reverses her wish because she wanted the wedding to happen.
why.She had already visited Kashi and needed: This contradicts the fact that she never made the visit.

activities.explanation: This is right because her choice puts the girl’s happiness above her own wish.

activities.prompt: Kashi Yatre first appeared as a serial. The novel described the old lady’s struggle. What can we infer?
options: Both forms carry the old lady’s wish and struggle to reach Kashi.
Both forms mainly show Kaveri reading to her grandmother.
Both forms end before the old lady begins her journey.
Both forms focus only on the orphan girl’s wedding.

why.Both forms mainly show Kaveri reading to: This wrongly treats the old woman’s story as a school story.
why.Both forms end before the old lady begin: This misreads a serial as a story that ends before it begins.
why.Both forms focus only on the orphan girl: This ignores the old lady’s journey and struggle to reach Kashi.

activities.explanation: This is right because both forms carry the old lady’s central story.

activities.prompt: The orphan girl is in love, but there is no money for her wedding. How does she most likely feel?
options: She worries about whether the wedding can happen.
She feels excited because the wedding will be easy.
She feels calm because money will not matter.
She blames the old lady for causing the wedding money problem.

why.She feels excited because the wedding wi: This confuses a money problem with an easy and happy wedding.
why.She feels calm because money will not ma: This wrongly assumes that she does not care about the wedding.
why.She blames the old lady for causing the: This misreads the old lady’s helpful choice as blame.

activities.explanation: This is right because the missing money puts her wish at risk.

activities.prompt: Kaveri reads each Wednesday’s episode to her grandmother. What does the grandmother’s later repetition show?
options: She listened closely and remembered the story very well.
She learned to read secretly during her school years.
She repeated sounds without understanding the story.
She understood the story but could not remember its words.

why.She learned to read secretly during her: This contradicts the fact that she never went to school.
why.She repeated sounds without understandin: This confuses remembering the words with not understanding them.
why.She understood the story but could not r: This wrongly says she forgot the words after understanding them.

activities.explanation: This is right because her exact repetition shows strong memory and attention.

activities.prompt: Kashi Yatre first came in parts. Each part led into the next. Which meaning of “serial” fits?
options: A story published in separate parts over time.
A complete story printed and sold only once.
A story about one person’s long journey.
A book that teaches lessons through many examples.

why.A complete story printed and sold only o: This describes a one-time book, not a story in parts.
This describes the old lady’s journey, not the serial form.
why.A book that teaches lessons through many: This describes a lesson book, not the way the story appeared.

activities.explanation: This is right because a serial is a story published in separate parts.

activities.prompt: The old lady gives up her wish to visit Kashi for the orphan girl. What lesson does this choice suggest?
options: Another person’s happiness can matter more than a personal wish.
A personal wish should always make other people unimportant.
A long journey matters more than helping someone in love.
Giving away savings always brings the giver a reward.

why.A personal wish should always make other: This wrongly makes a personal wish more important than another person.
why.A long journey matters more than helping: This reverses the choice because she helps the girl instead of travelling.
why.Giving away savings always brings the gi: This wrongly assumes that giving money always brings a reward.

activities.explanation: This is right because she chooses the girl’s happiness over her own wish.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: The Grandmother Waits for the Next Episode

activities.prompt: Why was Kaveri’s grandmother so eager for the next episode?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Waiting for the Story
activities.body: The grandmother saw herself as the novel’s main character. She wanted to know what would happen next more than anyone else. She always insisted that Kaveri read the serial to her. After each episode, she joined friends in the temple courtyard and discussed the story. Kaveri did not understand the debate. When she returned from a wedding, she found her grandmother in tears. Usually, her grandmother did not cry.
keyPoints: She saw herself as the novel’s main character.
She wanted to know what happened next.
She usually stayed calm during difficult situations.
activities.explanation: Good start! You know the grandmother’s strong interest in the story.

activities.prompt: Why was the grandmother crying when Kaveri came back?
steps: Kaveri stayed a week, so she did not read the serial.
The grandmother cared most about what would happen next.
She always wanted Kaveri to read the serial to her.
Her unusual tears show she felt upset about missing the story.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: The grandmother preferred to read the serial aloud to Kaveri.
activities.explanation: Not quite! She always insisted that Kaveri read the serial to her.

activities.prompt: Where did the grandmother join her friends after each episode?
options: At the wedding
In the temple courtyard
Beside Kaveri
With her cousins
activities.explanation: Yes! After each episode, she joined her friends in the temple courtyard.

activities.prompt: After each episode, she joined her friends in the ______ courtyard.
activities.hint: This is the place where her friends gathered.
activities.explanation: Well done! The courtyard was in the temple.

activities.prompt: Kaveri returned from the wedding. Why was she surprised to see her grandmother crying?
options: She never joined her friends.
She usually did not cry.
She had forgotten the serial.
She had stayed away.
activities.explanation: Good thinking! Her grandmother usually did not cry, even in difficult situations.

activities.prompt: Put these events in the correct order.
items: Kaveri attended the wedding with her cousins.
She stayed for a week instead of two days.
She returned and found her grandmother in tears.
Avva came and sat beside Kaveri that night.
activities.explanation: Correct! Kaveri attended the wedding, stayed longer, returned, and met Avva that night.

activities.prompt: Kaveri stayed at a wedding for a week. Her grandmother wanted to know what happened next. She always wanted Kaveri to read the serial. The grandmother was in tears when Kaveri returned. How did she most likely feel?
options: She felt upset about missing the story.
She felt angry about the long wedding.
She felt bored after waiting for a week.
She felt glad to see Kaveri again.

She wrongly thinks the wedding itself caused the tears.
She mistakes her sadness about the story for boredom.
She assumes happy tears, although she rarely cried.

activities.explanation: This fits her strong wish to know what happened next.

activities.prompt: After each episode, the grandmother joined her friends in the temple courtyard. She discussed the latest episode with them. What does this show about the story?
options: She thought the story was worth talking about.
She mainly wanted to meet her friends.
She thought the episode was completely boring.
She wanted Kaveri to read another episode.

She ignores her active discussion of each episode.
why.She thought the episode was completely b: This conflicts with her strong interest in the story.
why.She wanted Kaveri to read another episod: It mixes her reading habit with her courtyard activity.

activities.explanation: Her discussion shows that she valued the story.

activities.prompt: After each episode, the grandmother met her friends. She discussed the latest episode with them. She wanted to know what would happen next. What does 'episode' mean here?
options: One part of a story that continues.
One complete story with no later parts.
A family meeting held in a temple.
A long journey made by close friends.

It mistakes one episode for the whole story.
It connects the story part with the meeting place.
It invents a journey that the context does not show.

activities.explanation: The later parts show that the story continued.

activities.prompt: Kaveri found her grandmother in tears after returning from the wedding. The grandmother usually did not cry in difficult situations. Avva came and sat beside Kaveri that night. Why did Avva most likely sit beside her?
options: To give her comfort during a sad moment.
To ask Kaveri to read the serial.
To invite her to the temple courtyard.
To tell her friends about the wedding.

This uses the reading habit without explaining Avva's presence.
This guesses an invitation that the facts do not show.
This mistakes the visit for a message to friends.

activities.explanation: Sitting beside her showed care and support during a sad moment.

activities.prompt: The grandmother saw herself as the serial's main character. She was more interested than anyone in what happened next. How did she most likely see the serial?
options: Like a personal story that must keep going.
Like a boring story that should end soon.
Like a story that belonged only to Kaveri.
Like a story that her friends should ignore.

why.Like a boring story that should end soon: This conflicts with her great interest in the story.
why.Like a story that belonged only to Kaver: It mistakes Kaveri's role as reader for the grandmother's ownership.
why.Like a story that her friends should ign: It ignores the grandmother's habit of discussing it with friends.

activities.explanation: Her strong interest made the serial feel personal and continuing.

activities.prompt: Her grandmother and her friends discussed each episode. Kaveri did not understand why there was so much debate. What is the best lesson Kaveri could learn?
options: The serial was important to many people.
The serial was only a funny wedding story.
The serial mattered mainly to Kaveri.
The serial had no meaning for her friends.

why.The serial was only a funny wedding stor: It wrongly connects the serial with the wedding.
It reverses the facts because Kaveri did not understand the debate.
why.The serial had no meaning for her friend: It ignores the grandmother's repeated discussions with friends.

activities.explanation: Their repeated discussion shows that many people valued it.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: The Grandmother Tells Her Life Story

activities.prompt: What did the grandmother remember when she told Kaveri her life story?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: The Grandmother’s Life Story
activities.body: Grandmother’s childhood was hard. She lost her mother young. Nobody looked after or guided her. Her father married again. People did not think girls needed education. She married young, had children, and became busy. Cooking and feeding her family gave her happiness. Yet she sometimes wished she had gone to school. One summer night, the family slept on the terrace. Under a full moon, Kaveri’s grandmother told Kaveri her story.
keyPoints: Childhood loss and no guidance
Early marriage, children, and a busy life
Family happiness and regret about school
activities.explanation: You can follow the grandmother’s hardships, choices, and feelings.

activities.prompt: Why might she regret not going to school? Her family life made her happy.
steps: She lost her mother young, so nobody looked after her.
Girls were not thought to need school, so she missed it.
She married young, had children, and her life became busy.
She felt happy feeding her family, but sorry about missing school.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Where was the family sleeping on the summer night?
options: On the open terrace
Inside a closed room
Near the garden gate
Beside the kitchen fire
activities.explanation: The family was sleeping outside on the open terrace.

activities.prompt: The grandmother found great happiness in ______ and feeding her family.
activities.hint: She enjoyed preparing food for her family.
activities.explanation: Cooking and feeding her family brought the grandmother great happiness.

activities.prompt: Why did the young grandmother receive little guidance?
options: Her mother stayed close to her
Her teachers guided her daily
No one looked after her
Her father stayed close to her
activities.explanation: Nobody looked after or guided the young grandmother.

activities.prompt: Match each part of her life with the detail from her story.
pairs: She married very young and had children
She found great happiness in it
activities.explanation: These details show her family life, daily work, and feelings about school.

activities.prompt: She was always happy that she had never gone to school.
activities.explanation: She sometimes regretted not going to school. She also found joy in family life.

activities.prompt: Put these parts of the grandmother’s life in order.
items: She lost her mother as a young girl
Her father married again
She married very young
She had children and her life became busy
activities.explanation: These steps show her childhood, her father’s remarriage, and her own family life.

activities.prompt: Imagine a girl who loses her mother very young. Nobody guides her. How might she feel?
options: She may feel that nobody cared for her.
She may feel that her father always guided her.
She may feel that she had many helpers.
She may feel that her childhood was safe.

why.She may feel that her father always guid: This wrongly assumes that her father guided her.
This wrongly assumes that other helpers cared for her.
why.She may feel that her childhood was safe: This wrongly assumes that she felt safe without care.

activities.explanation: This fits because nobody looked after or guided her.

activities.prompt: People say girls do not need school. A girl marries young and has children. Why might she regret missing school?
options: She had no school or guidance as a girl.
She had many school choices after marriage.
She was always told to study at home.
Her father made school easy for her.

why.She had many school choices after marria: This wrongly assumes that marriage gave her school choices.
This wrongly assumes that people encouraged girls to study.
This wrongly assumes that her father made school easy.

activities.explanation: This fits because she had no school or guidance.

activities.prompt: Cooking and feeding her family gives a grandmother great joy. What does this show about her?
options: She values caring for her family through food.
She dislikes staying busy with her family.
She thinks education was never useful at all.
She wishes she had never married young.

why.She dislikes staying busy with her famil: This wrongly reads family care as dislike.
why.She thinks education was never useful at: This wrongly treats regret as saying school is useless.
This wrongly turns regret about school into regret about marriage.

activities.explanation: This fits because cooking and feeding her family brought joy.

activities.prompt: A twelve-year-old hears her sixty-two-year-old grandmother speak. Why might it feel strange?
options: Their ages show very different life stages.
The child and grandmother have the same age.
The grandmother has only a little experience.
The child's life is longer than her grandmother's.

why.The child and grandmother have the same: This wrongly assumes that both have the same age.
why.The grandmother has only a little experi: This wrongly assumes that age means little life experience.
why.The child's life is longer than her gran: This wrongly reverses who has lived longer.

activities.explanation: This fits because their ages show very different life stages.

activities.prompt: The family sleeps on an open terrace on a summer night. Why might she tell her story then?
options: The sleeping family gives her a quiet moment.
The full moon makes her childhood feel near.
The family is awake and asking many questions.
The summer heat makes her forget her life.

why.The full moon makes her childhood feel n: This wrongly treats moonlight as the reason she spoke.
why.The family is awake and asking many ques: This wrongly assumes that the family was awake.
why.The summer heat makes her forget her lif: This wrongly assumes that heat made her forget her life.

activities.explanation: This fits because the sleeping family gives her quiet time.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: A Decision to Learn

activities.prompt: What inspired a grandmother to begin learning Kannada?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A New Decision
activities.body: Grandmother tried to understand the magazine by rubbing its pages. She wished she had more education. She waited for Kaveri and felt very dependent and helpless. She felt that money could not make her independent. So she chose to learn the Kannada alphabet. Determination means a strong wish to keep trying. Kaveri noticed it on her face. Grandmother believed learning had no age limit.
keyPoints: She rubbed the magazine's pages.
She decided to learn the Kannada alphabet.
Learning had no age limit.
activities.explanation: Her wish to learn grew from her wish for education and independence.

activities.prompt: Why did the grandmother decide to learn Kannada instead of waiting for help?
steps: She tried to understand the magazine, but felt dependent and helpless.
She wished for education, so she wanted independence.
She was embarrassed to ask, so she decided to learn for herself.
She chose Kannada, with Saraswati Puja day during Dassara as her deadline.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What did Grandmother try to do by rubbing the magazine's pages?
options: Understand the magazine
Count all the pages
Find a hidden letter
Check each page number
activities.explanation: She rubbed her hands over the pages to understand the magazine.

activities.prompt: Grandmother rubbed the magazine's pages to understand it.
activities.explanation: She tried to understand the magazine by rubbing her hands over its pages.

activities.prompt: Grandmother decided to learn the ______ alphabet from the next day.
activities.hint: Choose the alphabet named in the lesson.
activities.explanation: She decided to learn the Kannada alphabet from the next day.

activities.prompt: Match each action or thought with its matching detail.
activities.explanation: Each pair connects Grandmother's action or thought with the matching part of the story.

activities.prompt: Which day did Grandmother choose as her deadline?
options: Saraswati Puja day
the next day
Kaveri's return day
the village day
activities.explanation: She chose Saraswati Puja day during Dassara as her deadline. The next day was when her learning began.

activities.prompt: Put Grandmother's feelings and decisions in the order they happened.
items: Feeling dependent and helpless
Feeling that money was useless
Deciding to learn the Kannada alphabet
Choosing Saraswati Puja day during Dassara
activities.explanation: Her feelings led to her decision. She then chose a clear deadline for learning.

activities.prompt: The grandmother rubbed the magazine's pages while trying to understand it. What did this action show?
options: She wanted to understand the magazine without asking for help.
She wanted to clean the magazine before reading it.
She wanted to hide the magazine from everyone.
She wanted to make sure the magazine stayed open.

why.She wanted to clean the magazine before: This mistake treats rubbing as cleaning, not a way to understand.
why.She wanted to hide the magazine from eve: This mistake imagines she wanted to hide the magazine.
why.She wanted to make sure the magazine sta: This mistake mistakes touching the pages for keeping it open.

activities.explanation: Rubbing the pages shows her own effort to understand the magazine.

activities.prompt: The grandmother wished she had received enough education. How did she feel about it?
options: She felt sorry that she had missed learning.
She felt happy that she had learned less.
She felt sure that education was a waste.
She felt afraid that she would learn too much.

why.She felt happy that she had learned less: This mistake reads regret about learning as happiness.
why.She felt sure that education was a waste: This mistake assumes she thought education was useless.
why.She felt afraid that she would learn too: This mistake mistakes regret about learning for fear of learning.

activities.explanation: Her wish shows regret about not receiving enough education.

activities.prompt: She waited eagerly for Kaveri to return. What did she most likely hope?
options: She hoped Kaveri would help her read the magazine.
She hoped Kaveri would bring her some books.
She hoped Kaveri would take her to the village.
She hoped Kaveri would choose her daily work.

why.She hoped Kaveri would bring her some bo: This mistake turns waiting for reading help into waiting for books.
why.She hoped Kaveri would take her to the v: This mistake confuses considering the village with her main hope.
why.She hoped Kaveri would choose her daily: This mistake adds a work plan not connected to the magazine.

activities.explanation: She wanted Kaveri to return so she could ask for reading help.

activities.prompt: She felt dependent and helpless without independence. What did she value most?
options: She valued being able to act for herself.
She valued owning more money than others.
She valued waiting for others to make choices.
She valued never needing to learn new things.

why.She valued owning more money than others: This mistake focuses on money instead of independence.
why.She valued waiting for others to make ch: This mistake confuses helplessness with a wish to wait.
why.She valued never needing to learn new th: This mistake confuses her choice to learn with avoiding learning.

activities.explanation: She felt money was useless while she could not be independent.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Learning, Independence and Respect

activities.prompt: How did teaching her grandmother change Kaveri’s life?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Kaveri's Student Becomes Independent
activities.body: Kaveri began teaching her grandmother the next day. Her grandmother became a wonderful student and completed homework. Lessons included reading, repeating, writing and reciting. Kaveri was her only teacher, and her grandmother was her first student. Kaveri later became a Computer Science teacher for hundreds of students. At Dassara, her grandmother gave frock material and touched Kaveri's feet. She said she respected Kaveri as her teacher and was now independent.
keyPoints: Kaveri taught reading, repeating, writing and reciting.
Her grandmother was Kaveri's first student.
Respect and independence grew through learning.
activities.explanation: Learning helped Kaveri's grandmother become independent and show respect.

activities.prompt: Can a person become independent after learning from a teacher?
steps: Kaveri taught reading, repeating, writing and reciting, so her grandmother could practise.
Her grandmother completed an amazing amount of homework, which showed serious effort.
Her independence and respect for Kaveri showed that the teaching had worked.
Thus, Kaveri helped her grandmother succeed and earned her respect.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: A Lesson Activity
activities.prompt: Her lessons included reading, repeating, writing and ______.
activities.hint: Choose one lesson activity.
activities.explanation: Reciting was one of the lesson activities.

activities.title: A Special Gift
activities.prompt: What did Kaveri's grandmother give Kaveri at Dassara?
options: frock material
a pen
a cake
a textbook
activities.explanation: She gave Kaveri frock material as a gift.

activities.title: Match the Details
activities.prompt: Match each detail with its correct answer.
activities.explanation: These details show the people, subject and festival in the lesson.

activities.title: Showing Respect
activities.prompt: What did Kaveri's grandmother do to show respect for her teacher?
options: Touched Kaveri's feet
Gave Kaveri homework
Began a lesson
Wrote a letter
activities.explanation: She touched Kaveri's feet because she respected her as her teacher.

activities.title: A Successful Student
activities.prompt: Kaveri knew that her student had succeeded very well. What did the grandmother say she was now?
options: independent
a computer teacher
a festival guest
a young student
activities.explanation: The grandmother said that she was now independent, and Kaveri knew her student had succeeded.

activities.title: Follow Kaveri's Journey
activities.prompt: Put these events in order.
items: Kaveri taught her grandmother
Her grandmother completed her homework
Kaveri became a Computer Science teacher
activities.explanation: Kaveri began teaching first, and she became a Computer Science teacher later.

activities.prompt: Kaveri's grandmother completed an amazing amount of homework. How did Kaveri most likely feel?
options: Proud of her student's great success
Worried about her student's great success
Angry about her student's great success
Disappointed by her student's great success

why.Worried about her student's great succes: This mistakes success for worry, but nothing shows Kaveri was worried.
why.Angry about her student's great success: This mistakes success for anger, but no anger is shown.
why.Disappointed by her student's great succ: This mistakes success for disappointment, but Kaveri was pleased.

activities.explanation: This fits because Kaveri knew her student had succeeded very well.

activities.prompt: Kaveri's grandmother said that she was now independent after her lessons. What did this word mean here?
options: She could learn and act on her own
She no longer needed to learn anything
She had become Kaveri's only teacher
She had stopped doing all her homework

why.She no longer needed to learn anything: This wrongly thinks independence means never learning again.
why.She had become Kaveri's only teacher: This reverses their roles, but Kaveri remained the teacher.
why.She had stopped doing all her homework: This wrongly thinks independence means stopping all work.

activities.explanation: Independent means able to learn and act by herself.

activities.prompt: The grandmother bent down and touched Kaveri's feet. What did this action most strongly show?
options: That Kaveri was her first student
Respect for Kaveri as her teacher
That she wanted to avoid all lessons
That she was angry with Kaveri

why.That Kaveri was her first student: She explained that she was respecting Kaveri as her teacher.
why.That she wanted to avoid all lessons: This mistakes a respectful gesture for a wish to avoid lessons.
why.That she was angry with Kaveri: This invents anger, but the gesture showed respect.

activities.explanation: This confuses the gesture with their earlier student-teacher roles.

activities.prompt: The Dassara festival arrived, and her grandmother gave Kaveri frock material. What did the gift most likely show?
options: She disliked Kaveri and wanted to leave
She feared Kaveri and avoided all lessons
She appreciated Kaveri's teaching and felt grateful
She wanted Kaveri to become her student

why.She disliked Kaveri and wanted to leave: The gift and her later respect suggest gratitude for Kaveri's teaching.
why.She feared Kaveri and avoided all lesson: This wrongly treats a gift as a sign of dislike.
why.She wanted Kaveri to become her student: This reverses their roles, but Kaveri was the teacher.

activities.explanation: This wrongly treats a gift as a sign of fear.

activities.prompt: Kaveri was her grandmother's only teacher. Her grandmother was her first student. Later, she taught Computer Science to hundreds. What does this show?
options: Her teaching began with many students and later reached her grandmother
Her teaching always involved only her grandmother at home
Her teaching ended before she became a Computer Science teacher
Her teaching began with her grandmother and later reached many students

why.Her teaching began with many students an: Her grandmother was her first student, and later she taught hundreds.
why.Her teaching always involved only her gr: This reverses the order of the two stages.
why.Her teaching ended before she became a C: This ignores that she later became a Computer Science teacher.

activities.explanation: It follows the order from her grandmother to hundreds of students.

activities.context: Kaveri lived with her grandparents in a north Karnataka village. Because transport was poor, the family got the morning paper only in the afternoon, while the weekly magazine came a day late. Everyone waited eagerly for the bus, which brought newspapers, magazines and the post. Triveni’s Kannada stories were easy to read, convincing and very interesting. They dealt with difficult problems in ordinary lives, and people continued to appreciate her novels forty years after her death.
activities.prompt: Why did Kaveri’s family receive the morning paper only in the afternoon?
options: The delayed journey of the papers through the village transport system caused the late delivery.
The publisher deliberately sent the morning paper to the grandparents’ home after lunch.
The family’s habit of waiting for the bus made the publisher choose afternoon delivery.
The weekly magazine was routinely held back until the day before the bus came.

why.The publisher deliberately sent the morn: There is no fact suggesting a deliberate afternoon delivery.
why.The family’s habit of waiting for the bu: The publisher’s delivery time was not based on the family’s waiting habit.
why.The weekly magazine was routinely held b: The weekly magazine was one day late, not deliberately held back.

activities.explanation: The poor transport system delayed newspapers reaching the village.

activities.context: Kaveri lived with her grandparents in a north Karnataka village. Because transport was poor, the family got the morning paper only in the afternoon, while the weekly magazine came a day late. Everyone waited eagerly for the bus, which brought newspapers, magazines and the post. Triveni’s Kannada stories were easy to read, convincing and very interesting. They dealt with difficult problems in ordinary lives, and people continued to appreciate her novels forty years after her death.
activities.prompt: If the bus reached Kaveri’s family earlier, what would be the most reasonable result?
options: The family would probably receive the newspapers and weekly magazine sooner.
The family would probably continue to receive the morning paper only in the afternoon.
The family would probably receive the newspapers and weekly magazine later than before.
The family would probably have to wait longer for the bus to arrive.

why.The family would probably continue to re: An improved journey would be unlikely to preserve the afternoon delay.
why.The family would probably receive the ne: This outcome reverses the likely effect of an earlier bus.
why.The family would probably have to wait l: Reaching the family earlier would not normally require a longer wait.

activities.explanation: Earlier arrival by the bus would normally mean earlier delivery of its cargo.

activities.context: Kaveri lived with her grandparents in a north Karnataka village. Because transport was poor, the family got the morning paper only in the afternoon, while the weekly magazine came a day late. Everyone waited eagerly for the bus, which brought newspapers, magazines and the post. Triveni’s Kannada stories were easy to read, convincing and very interesting. They dealt with difficult problems in ordinary lives, and people continued to appreciate her novels forty years after her death.
activities.prompt: Why is a Triveni novel likely to interest Kaveri?
options: Her writing is easy to follow and convincing, and it presents interesting stories about difficult problems faced by ordinary people.
Her novels are attractive only to readers who do not understand difficult problems.
Her novels discuss ordinary lives but avoid the problems that ordinary people face.
Her convincing writing would have little value if her stories did not interest readers.

why.Her novels are attractive only to reader: Her work was not limited to readers who avoided difficult subjects.
why.Her novels discuss ordinary lives but av: Her stories actually dealt with difficult problems in ordinary lives.
why.Her convincing writing would have little: Her convincing style was one reason her interesting stories could appeal to readers.

activities.explanation: Triveni’s readable and convincing stories always held readers’ attention.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): Kaveri’s family received the morning paper only in the afternoon.
Reason (R): The village’s poor transport system delayed the arrival of newspapers.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: The poor transport system directly explains why the family received the newspaper late.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): People continued to appreciate Triveni’s novels forty years after her death.
Reason (R): The weekly magazine arrived one day late in Kaveri’s village.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: Both statements are true, but the magazine’s delay does not explain the continuing appreciation of Triveni’s novels.

activities.prompt: How did Triveni’s writing make ordinary people’s problems interesting, and why did her novels remain valued after her early death?
activities.answer: Triveni’s writing made difficult problems in ordinary lives easy to read and convincing. Her stories were always very interesting, so readers could engage with serious difficulties in the lives of ordinary people. Triveni died when she was very young, but people continued to appreciate her novels forty years later. The lasting appeal of her work came from her readable and convincing style, her interesting stories and her focus on the difficult problems faced by ordinary people.
points: Triveni’s writing style was easy to read and convincing.
Her stories were always very interesting.
She dealt with difficult problems in ordinary people’s lives.
Her novels were still appreciated forty years after her death.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Kaveri reads the next episode of Kashi Yatre to Krishtakka every Wednesday. Although Krishtakka has never been to school and cannot read, she later repeats the whole text from memory. The serial concerns an old lady who strongly wishes to visit Kashi or Varanasi. The novel describes her struggle to reach Kashi and shows an orphan girl falling in love, with no money for the orphan’s wedding. The old lady gives away all her savings without visiting.
activities.prompt: If the next Wednesday episode has not yet arrived, what should Kaveri do?
options: Wait for the episode and read it aloud to Krishtakka.
Ask Krishtakka to read the next episode aloud herself.
Guess the episode and present the guess as Kaveri’s reading.
Ask Krishtakka to repeat the previous episode until the new one arrives.

why.Ask Krishtakka to read the next episode: This reverses their roles because Krishtakka cannot read.
why.Guess the episode and present the guess: A guessed episode is not the actual text in the magazine.
why.Ask Krishtakka to repeat the previous ep: Repeating the previous episode does not help read the new one.

activities.explanation: This is correct because Kaveri is the person who reads the episodes.

activities.context: Kaveri reads the next episode of Kashi Yatre to Krishtakka every Wednesday. Although Krishtakka has never been to school and cannot read, she later repeats the whole text from memory. The serial concerns an old lady who strongly wishes to visit Kashi or Varanasi. The novel describes her struggle to reach Kashi and shows an orphan girl falling in love, with no money for the orphan’s wedding. The old lady gives away all her savings without visiting.
activities.prompt: Why was Krishtakka able to repeat the whole text later?
options: She listened to Kaveri’s reading and retained what she heard.
She secretly learned to read from the magazine.
She had already read the same episode at school.
She used another copy of the magazine to read the text later.

why.She secretly learned to read from the ma: This assumes that Krishtakka learned to read despite being unable to read.
why.She had already read the same episode at: This contradicts the fact that she had never been to school.
why.She used another copy of the magazine to: This assumes reading ability that Krishtakka did not possess.

activities.explanation: Kaveri read aloud, and Krishtakka later remembered the text.

activities.context: Kaveri reads the next episode of Kashi Yatre to Krishtakka every Wednesday. Although Krishtakka has never been to school and cannot read, she later repeats the whole text from memory. The serial concerns an old lady who strongly wishes to visit Kashi or Varanasi. The novel describes her struggle to reach Kashi and shows an orphan girl falling in love, with no money for the orphan’s wedding. The old lady gives away all her savings without visiting.
activities.prompt: If the old lady had valued her own visit to Kashi above the orphan girl’s happiness, what would she most likely have done with her savings?
options: Keep the savings for her own journey to Kashi.
Give the savings toward the orphan girl’s wedding.
Give the savings to another person hoping to visit Kashi.
Hide the savings and continue hoping to visit Kashi.

why.Give the savings toward the orphan girl’: This would continue her original choice to value the orphan girl’s happiness.
why.Give the savings to another person hopin: Giving money to someone else would not prioritize her own journey.
why.Hide the savings and continue hoping to: Hiding the savings would postpone rather than support her visit.

activities.explanation: The changed priority would make her own journey more important.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): The old lady regarded the orphan girl’s happiness as more important than worship at Kashi.
Reason (R): The old lady wanted the orphan girl to remain unhappy so that she would visit Kashi herself.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: The proposed reason is false because the old lady valued the orphan girl’s happiness.

activities.prompt: Explain how Kaveri helped Krishtakka follow and remember the serial.
activities.answer: The magazine came every Wednesday, and Kaveri read the next episode of Kashi Yatre to Krishtakka. This gave her grandmother access to the story even though she had never been to school and could not read. By listening to Kaveri, Krishtakka was able to remember the episode. Her later ability to repeat the whole text from memory shows that she had followed the reading closely. In this way, Kaveri helped her grandmother follow the serial and retain its words without learning to read them herself.
points: Kaveri read the next episode every Wednesday.
Krishtakka had never been to school and could not read.
Listening helped Krishtakka remember the episode.
She later repeated the whole text from memory.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: Kaveri attended a wedding with her cousins. A wedding was regarded as a great event in those days. Kaveri planned to stay for two days, but she remained for a week. When she returned, she found her grandmother in tears, even though the grandmother seldom cried in difficult moments. Avva came and sat beside Kaveri. The grandmother saw herself as the serial's main character, wanted Kaveri to read it, and was eager to learn what would happen next.
activities.prompt: Why was Kaveri's week-long absence likely to matter especially to her grandmother?
options: The grandmother had a stronger interest in the novel than anyone else and had been waiting for Kaveri to read it.
The grandmother had expected to attend the wedding with Kaveri and felt abandoned.
The grandmother was angry because the wedding lasted longer than planned.
The grandmother was confused because her friends discussed the story without explaining it to her.

why.The grandmother had expected to attend t: There is no fact suggesting that the grandmother expected to attend the wedding.
why.The grandmother was angry because the we: The grandmother did not plan the wedding or decide how long Kaveri would stay.
why.The grandmother was confused because her: The grandmother herself joined her friends and discussed each episode with them.

activities.explanation: This directly connects the grandmother's intense interest with Kaveri's absence.

activities.context: Kaveri attended a wedding with her cousins. A wedding was regarded as a great event in those days. Kaveri planned to stay for two days, but she remained for a week. When she returned, she found her grandmother in tears, even though the grandmother seldom cried in difficult moments. Avva came and sat beside Kaveri. The grandmother saw herself as the serial's main character, wanted Kaveri to read it, and was eager to learn what would happen next.
activities.prompt: When Kaveri meets her grandmother after returning from the wedding, what is the grandmother most likely to request?
options: Read the latest episode aloud to her.
Explain why the wedding lasted for a week.
Take her to the temple courtyard immediately.
Discuss why everybody had argued about the story.

why.Explain why the wedding lasted for a wee: The wedding's length was Kaveri's decision, not a matter for the grandmother.
why.Take her to the temple courtyard immedia: The grandmother normally joined her friends there after an episode.
why.Discuss why everybody had argued about t: Kaveri, rather than the grandmother, was the one who did not understand the debate.

activities.explanation: The grandmother always wanted Kaveri to read the serial to her.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): The grandmother saw herself as the novel's main character.
Reason (R): Because of this view of herself, she was more interested than anyone else in knowing what would happen next.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: Her belief that she was the main character explains her exceptional interest in the story's next event.

activities.prompt:
Assertion (A): Kaveri did not understand why there was so much debate about the story.
Reason (R): Kaveri had attended a wedding with her cousins and remained there for a week.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
activities.explanation: The wedding trip is true, but it does not explain why Kaveri failed to understand the debate.

activities.prompt: Explain why the grandmother's behaviour shows that she had become deeply involved in the novel.
activities.answer: The grandmother's behaviour shows that she had become deeply involved in the novel because she saw herself as its main character. She was more interested than anyone else in knowing what would happen next, and she always insisted that Kaveri read the serial to her. After each episode, she joined her friends in the temple courtyard and discussed it with them. Her involvement was therefore not limited to hearing the story; it also shaped her conversations with her friends and the way she spent her time after an episode.
points: She saw herself as the novel's main character.
She was especially eager to know what would happen next.
She always insisted that Kaveri read the serial.
She discussed each episode with her friends in the temple courtyard.
activities.explanation: Compare your answer with the points a marker looks for.

activities.context: During a summer night, the family slept on the open terrace under a full moon. A sixty-two-year-old grandmother told the story of her life late at night to the twelve-year-old narrator, who found it strange. She said that she had lost her mother as a young girl, received no guidance, and married very young. Her father remarried. Cooking for her busy family brought her great happiness, though she sometimes regretted not attending school. She affectionately touched Kaveri’s forehead.
activities.prompt: If people had believed that girls needed education and had allowed the young grandmother to attend school, what would most likely have changed?
options: She might have attended school and felt less regret about her own education.
She might have married much later and had no children.
Her life might have become completely free of family responsibilities.
She might have found less happiness in preparing meals for her family.

why.She might have married much later and ha: A later marriage is possible, but having no children does not follow.
why.Her life might have become completely fr: Education would not remove every family responsibility.
why.She might have found less happiness in p: Her happiness in preparing meals would not necessarily change.

activities.explanation: Attending school would directly affect her later regret about her education.

activities.context: During a summer night, the family slept on the open terrace under a full moon. A sixty-two-year-old grandmother told the story of her life late at night to the twelve-year-old narrator, who found it strange. options: Preparing meals for her family gave her deep satisfaction.
Her main happiness came from having plenty of leisure time.
She was happy because she had received a good education.
She was unhappy because her family did not appreciate her cooking.

why.Her main happiness came from having plen: Her life was busy, so leisure was not the source of her happiness.
why.She was happy because she had received a: She sometimes regretted not attending school.
why.She was unhappy because her family did n: She found great happiness in cooking for her family.

activities.explanation: Preparing food and feeding her family were a genuine source of happiness.

chapters.title: The Pot Maker
chapters.summary: In this chapter: a hidden dream; arenla’s choice of weaving; a skill shared by the village; learning from her mother.

lessons.title: A Hidden Dream

activities.prompt: What was Sentila secretly dreaming of becoming?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Sentila's Hidden Dream
activities.body: Sentila dreamed of becoming a pot maker. Her mother and grandmother made pots. Arenla wanted her to become a weaver, someone who makes cloth. Sentila kept her dream secret at home. She quietly approached skilled potters to learn. They thought she would soon lose interest. But she stayed interested and kept watching their work. She learned how they prepared clay.
keyPoints: Sentila dreamed of making pots.
She kept this dream secret at home.
She continued learning from expert potters.
activities.explanation: Sentila stayed interested in her dream and quietly learned from expert potters.

activities.prompt: Why did Sentila keep her pottery dream secret and keep learning?
steps: Sentila loved pot making, like her mother and grandmother.
Arenla wanted her to become a weaver, not a pot maker.
So she approached potters secretly and kept her fascination at home.
Her continued watching showed that her interest did not fade.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Who Inspired the Dream?
activities.prompt: Who inspired Sentila's dream of becoming a pot maker?
options: Her mother and grandmother
Arenla and her teacher
The expert potters
Her neighbours
activities.explanation: Sentila wanted to become a pot maker like her mother and grandmother.

activities.prompt: Arenla wanted Sentila to become a weaver.
activities.explanation: Arenla wanted Sentila to follow a different craft and become a weaver.

activities.title: What Did the Potters Expect?
activities.prompt: What did the expert potters expect Sentila to do?
options: Become a skilled pot maker
Lose interest in pottery
Become a weaver
Leave the village
activities.explanation: The potters thought Sentila would soon lose interest in making pots.

activities.title: Prepare the Clay
activities.prompt: Put the potters' clay-making steps in order.
items: Mix the clay with water
Pound the clay
Push left hands into softened clay
activities.explanation: The lesson lists mixing and pounding first. It then describes pushing left hands into softened clay.

activities.title: A Different Choice
activities.prompt: Which choice best shows that Sentila did not lose interest in pottery?
options: She kept watching and learning.
She stopped after Arenla complained.
She chose weaving at once.
She gave up her dream.
activities.explanation: Sentila kept watching the potters and learning. This showed that her interest in pottery lasted.

activities.prompt: You want to make pots. Your family expects you to weave. Why hide this dream?
options: You love pot making and want to learn it.
You dislike weaving and want to leave home.
You expect weaving to become boring very soon.
You plan to teach weaving to every potter.

why.You dislike weaving and want to leave ho: This mistakes dislike of weaving for her reason to hide.
why.You expect weaving to become boring very: This wrongly assumes she already expects to lose interest.
why.You plan to teach weaving to every potte: This confuses her goal with a wish to teach weaving.

activities.explanation: This is right because her pot-making dream explains her secrecy.

activities.prompt: The potters expected Sentila to lose interest. She kept watching them. What does this show?
options: Her interest in pottery has stayed strong.
Her interest in pottery has quickly vanished.
You want weaving to become your only work.
You learned nothing by watching expert potters.

why.Her interest in pottery has quickly vani: This mistakes continued watching for a vanished interest.
why.You want weaving to become your only wor: This adds a wish for weaving that the story does not show.
why.You learned nothing by watching expert p: This mistakes watching for failure to learn anything.

activities.explanation: This is right because her continued watching shows lasting interest.

activities.prompt: The potters mix clay with water and pound it. Sentila puts her hand into softened clay. What is she trying to learn?
options: She is learning pottery by handling the clay.
She is refusing to learn how pots are made.
She is mixing clay only to make mud.
She is checking whether clay feels like water.

why.She is refusing to learn how pots are ma: This mistakes active learning for a refusal to learn.
This mistakes practice with clay for simply making mud.
why.She is checking whether clay feels like: This guesses a water test that the story does not mention.

activities.explanation: This is right because handling clay is direct pottery practice.

activities.prompt: Sentila wants to make pots. Arenla wants her to weave. Why might she stay silent?
options: She feels caught between her dream and Arenla's wish.
She feels excited to discuss weaving with Arenla.
She feels sure that weaving is already her dream.
She feels calm because pottery no longer matters.

why.She feels excited to discuss weaving wit: This wrongly treats the complaint as a happy weaving discussion.
why.She feels sure that weaving is already h: This confuses Arenla's wish with Sentila's own dream.
why.She feels calm because pottery no longer: This mistakes hidden love for pottery for no interest.

activities.explanation: This is right because her dream and Arenla's wish pull her differently.

activities.prompt: Sentila's mother and grandmother make pots. Sentila dreams of becoming one. What likely helped shape her dream?
options: Growing up around her family's pottery work.
Arenla's repeated complaint about her weaving.
The potters' belief that she would quit.
Her first feeling of touching softened clay.

why.Arenla's repeated complaint about her we: This wrongly makes Arenla's complaint the cause of her dream.
This reverses cause and effect by making doubt encouraging.
why.Her first feeling of touching softened c: This wrongly links her dream to an early clay touch.

activities.explanation: This is right because family examples likely shaped her choice.

lessons.title: Arenla’s Choice of Weaving

activities.prompt: What choice could bring more comfort to Arenla’s family?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Arenla’s tiring work
activities.body: Arenla’s work with clay was tiring. She had to reach riverbank clay, carry heavy loads uphill, and pound clay in bamboo cylinders. She often dropped the mould because she was exhausted. A batch of pots took several months to finish, but she received only a few rupees. Learning weaving could earn more money and provide cloth for the family. Weaving could be done indoors in every season.
keyPoints: Arenla found clay work tiring.
A batch of pots took several months to finish.
Weaving could earn more money and provide cloth for the family.
activities.explanation: Arenla chose weaving because it offered better rewards and could be done indoors.

activities.prompt: Arenla must choose between making clay pots and learning to weave. Which work should she choose, and why?
steps: Pot-making is tiring because Arenla carries heavy loads uphill.
It also takes months, but pays only a few rupees.
Weaving could bring more money and cloth for her family.
Weaving is better because it takes less time and can be done indoors in every season.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Why weaving helped
activities.body: Choosing weaving meant looking for a way to earn more and help her family. It could provide cloth for the family, and it could be done indoors in every season. Making one shawl took less time than making a batch of pots. These points explain why weaving was a helpful choice for Arenla.
keyPoints: Weaving could provide cloth for the family.
Weaving could be done indoors in every season.
Making one shawl took less time than making a batch of pots.
activities.explanation: Weaving offered money, cloth, and work that could continue in every season.

activities.prompt: Why did Arenla’s back ache?
options: Because she carried heavy loads downhill.
Because she carried heavy loads uphill.
Because she carried light loads to school.
Because she carried empty baskets uphill.
activities.explanation: Arenla’s back ached because she carried heavy loads uphill.

activities.prompt: Arenla often dropped the mould because she felt energetic.
activities.explanation: She often dropped the mould because she was exhausted.

activities.prompt: Arenla received only a few ______ for all that work.
activities.hint: This is the name of the money she received.
activities.explanation: Arenla received only a few rupees for all her clay work.

activities.prompt: Making one shawl took less time than making a batch of pots.
activities.explanation: The lesson says that making one shawl took less time than making a batch of pots.

activities.prompt: Match each part of Arenla’s clay work with its result.
activities.explanation: Each result is connected to the part of Arenla’s tiring clay work.

activities.prompt: Which task took less time according to the lesson?
options: Making a batch of pots
Making one shawl
Pounding clay in bamboo cylinders
Carrying heavy loads uphill
activities.explanation: Making one shawl took less time than making a batch of pots.

activities.prompt: Arenla climbs down a steep drop and carries heavy clay uphill. She often drops the mould. What does this show?
options: She is too exhausted to keep holding it.
She wants to start making shawls.
She thinks the riverbank is too far.
She has already finished a batch of pots.

This wrongly treats a future plan as the reason for her exhaustion.
This mistakes the clay's distance for the reason she drops it.
why.She has already finished a batch of pots: This wrongly assumes that dropping the mould means the work is finished.

activities.explanation: This is right because exhaustion makes her drop the mould.

activities.prompt: Weaving can bring more money and cloth to Arenla's family. It can also be done indoors in every season. Why might she choose weaving?
options: It can help her family and earn more money.
It can keep her working outdoors in summer.
It always takes more time than making pots.
It needs no effort from her at all.

why.It can keep her working outdoors in summ: This reverses the fact that weaving can be done indoors.
why.It always takes more time than making po: This reverses the fact that a shawl takes less time than a batch of pots.
This wrongly treats earning money as needing no work.

activities.explanation: This is right because weaving can earn more money and provide cloth.

activities.prompt: Arenla spends months making a batch of pots. She receives only a few rupees for the work. How might she feel?
options: She may feel the effort was not worth it.
She may feel pleased to rest from weaving.
She may expect many more months of work.
She may think the pots were made too quickly.

why.She may feel pleased to rest from weavin: Nothing says weaving has tired her or that she feels rested.
A small payment does not show that she expects many more months.
why.She may think the pots were made too qui: Several months show slow work, not work made too quickly.

activities.explanation: This is right because months of work for few rupees seems a poor return.

activities.prompt: One shawl takes less time than a batch of pots. Weaving can be done indoors in every season. What does this suggest?
options: Arenla may have more time for weaving.
Weaving must always be done beside a river.
Pot-making is the only work done indoors.
Arenla will never need to carry heavy loads.

why.Weaving must always be done beside a riv: This wrongly places weaving outdoors beside a river.
why.Pot-making is the only work done indoors: This wrongly assumes that all indoor work must be weaving.
why.Arenla will never need to carry heavy lo: Indoor weaving does not prove that she will carry nothing.

activities.explanation: This is right because making a shawl takes less time than making pots.

activities.prompt: Arenla needs several months to finish her batch of pots. What does the word "batch" mean here?
options: A group of pots made together.
One pot made in a few minutes.
A roll of cloth for one shawl.
A long trip to the riverbank.

This wrongly treats the batch as a single quick pot.
This mixes up pots with weaving materials.
This mistakes a group of work for a journey.

activities.explanation: This is right because the batch is the group of pots she makes.

activities.prompt: Arenla reaches the riverbank by climbing down a steep drop. She carries heavy loads back uphill, and her back aches. Why does her back hurt?
options: The heavy uphill carrying strains her back.
The clay is too far from the village.
The bamboo cylinders are too small.
Making one shawl has tired her back.

This mistakes the distance for the cause of her back pain.
Nothing in the facts says that the bamboo cylinders are too small.
This wrongly links her pain to weaving instead of carrying clay.

activities.explanation: This is right because heavy loads uphill cause her back to ache.

lessons.title: A Skill Shared by the Village

activities.prompt: How can a village keep an ancient pottery skill alive for future generations?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: A Village Skill for Everyone
activities.body: Pottery was a shared village skill, not the secret of one person. Each potter gave a final touch to keep its shape. Pots dried in the sun before they went to the kiln for firing. Firing them too much or too little could ruin a whole batch. Experts were expected to teach anyone who wished to learn. So knowledge could pass from one learner to another.
keyPoints: Potters carefully shaped and dried each pot.
Bad firing could ruin a whole batch.
Experts should pass on traditional skills.
activities.explanation: Sharing skills helped the village continue its pottery tradition.

activities.prompt: Sentila visits expert potters. Villagers worry about future experts. How should the village handle teaching?
steps: Pottery requires careful work because over-firing or under-firing can ruin a whole batch.
Sentila’s visits cause gossip, so villagers worry that present experts may lack replacements.
The council questions Mesoba because Arenla’s duty to teach Sentila is at issue.
The council says skills belong to everyone, so experts should teach any willing learner.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: Match each pottery action with its result.
pairs: Gave each pot a final touch
Dried the pots in the sun
activities.explanation: Each step mattered. A careful touch, sun-drying and correct firing protected the pots.

activities.prompt: The potters dried each pot in the sun before taking it to the kiln.
activities.explanation: Pots were dried in the sun first. Then, they were taken to the kiln.

activities.prompt: Put the council's events in the order they happened.
items: The village council summoned Mesoba.
Mesoba said Arenla had never refused to teach Sentila.
The council reminded Mesoba about Arenla's duty.
The council said traditional skills did not belong to one person.
activities.explanation: The meeting began with the summons. Mesoba spoke, and then the council gave its reminders.

activities.prompt: What did Mesoba say about Arenla and teaching Sentila?
options: Arenla had taught Sentila only once.
Arenla had planned to refuse Mesoba.
Arenla had never refused to teach Sentila.
Arenla had asked the council for help.
activities.explanation: Mesoba clearly said that Arenla had never refused to teach Sentila.

activities.prompt: What were expert potters expected to do?
options: Pass their skills to new learners
Keep their skills within workshops
Teach only their own children
Wait for expert potters to leave
activities.explanation: Experts were expected to pass their skills to anyone who wished to learn.

activities.prompt: What did the village notice and worry about as Sentila learned?
options: Visits became gossip; new experts might replace the present potters.
Visits became gossip; no experts might replace the present potters.
Visits stayed secret; no experts might replace the present potters.
Visits became gossip; the council stopped all teaching.
activities.explanation: Sentila's visits became village gossip. The villagers also worried about having no expert potters to replace the present ones.

activities.prompt: The village council summons Mesoba for questioning. What does this action show?
options: The council wants to discuss Sentila's teaching.
The council wants to end all visits to potters.
The council wants to close the village kiln.
The council wants to stop pottery teaching.

why.The council wants to end all visits to p: This mistakes one meeting for a decision to stop visits.
why.The council wants to close the village k: This mistakes a question about teaching for a kiln decision.
why.The council wants to stop pottery teachi: This mistakes checking the teaching for a decision to stop it.

activities.explanation: The questioning concerns Mesoba's answer about Arenla teaching Sentila.

activities.prompt: Mesoba says Arenla never refused to teach Sentila. How does he seem to feel?
options: He seems to defend Arenla against blame.
He seems to agree that Arenla refused.
He seems excited about village gossip.
He seems eager to end pottery lessons.

This mistakes his defence for agreement with the blame.
This mistakes his serious answer for excitement about gossip.
This mistakes his defence as a wish to stop teaching.

activities.explanation: His answer supports Arenla and rejects the idea that she refused.

activities.prompt: The council says traditional skills do not belong to one person. What should an expert do?
options: Teach any willing person who wants to learn.
Keep the skill within one family only.
Wait until no learner remains willing.
Refuse every learner who asks for help.

This treats a shared skill as belonging to one family.
This delays teaching even though willing learners exist.
This keeps the skill from those who wish to learn it.

activities.explanation: Experts are expected to pass their skills to anyone willing to learn.
